elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4(a): "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient." A convenience right exists (subject to the retained 12-month Initial Term lock-out, which is a noted limitation rather than an absent right; there are no Order Forms in this structure).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The Customer right runs on "ninety (90) days written notice", not 30 days. To reach preferred the drafter would have to change Customer's notice figure to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere; the retained sentence runs the other way — "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates". A pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation would have to be inserted.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "Kubient may terminate this Agreement upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer, effective only at the end of the then-current Term." The effective date is expressly tied to the term boundary, so no mid-term Vendor exit survives; 4(b) exits are for cause/insolvency, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — an unconditional Customer election at 90 days, at the top of the 60–90 band.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The only payment mechanic on exit is the retained "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" — i.e. ordinary fees accruing over the 90-day notice period, with no separate penalty or acceleration. Whether read as no early-termination fee at all (condition inapplicable) or as a fee bounded by the 90-day period, it does not exceed three months of fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: New sentence expressly ties the effective date to the boundary: "effective only at the end of the then-current Term", satisfying the requirement that a Vendor notice right be term-end-only rather than a mid-term exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may terminate this Agreement upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer" — exactly the 90-day floor.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Customer 90-day convenience right, no early-termination fee beyond fees accruing in the 90-day notice period, Vendor termination expressly effective only at the end of the then-current Term, and a 90-day Vendor notice floor.

Preferred is not reached on two elements: Customer notice remains 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund (the retained sentence in fact entitles Kubient to fees generated during the termination period). Both are correctly left unpursued given the fallback is met.

Deviation classification is sound: the original mutual "for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" let Kubient exit at any point inside a renewal term, which is a mid-term Vendor convenience exit and fails the fallback's term-end-only requirement; it is not natural-term non-renewal.

Minimal: the edit splits one sentence into two party-specific sentences and adds only the term-end effectiveness qualifier needed for the failing element. The Initial Term lock-out, the fee-entitlement sentence, and all of 4(b) are retained verbatim; no survival tails, refund mechanics, or extra procedures were added.

Preserves intent: no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created ("Term" and "Initial Term" are both defined in the same paragraph), the breach and insolvency exits are untouched, and the commercial fee allocation on exit is unchanged.

Minor point the drafter may wish to tidy (not a failure): the new Kubient sentence drops the words "for any reason" and does not repeat "following the Initial Term", relying on the retained "Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term" sentence; the two read consistently because a notice effective at a term boundary is not a termination occurring during the Initial Term, but adding "for any reason" would remove any argument that the sentence is a separate cause-based right.
